in_arabic.name: بوديد

in_urdu.name: بدید
in_urdu.long_meaning: یہ نام 'بدد' کے جذر سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے بکھرنا یا تفرق کرنا۔ یہ ممکن ہے کہ اس کا تعلق کسی چیز کی کمی یا صغر سے ہو۔ اسلامی تقالید میں اس کا استعمال شائع ہے۔

in_hindi.name: बुदैद
in_hindi.long_meaning: यह नाम 'بدد' के मूल से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है बिखरना या अलग होना। यह किसी चीज़ की कम मात्रा या छोटेपन को दर्शाता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इसका उपयोग पारंपरिक है।

in_pashto.name: بوديد
in_pashto.long_meaning: دا نوم د 'بدد' جذر څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې د بې ځایه کیدل یا توپیر کول دي. دا ممکنه ده چې د لږ یا کوچني کیدو سره تړاو ولري. په افغان او پښتون قومونو کې کارول کیږي.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Budaid" holds a special place in Islamic culture, as it reflects a trait that is highly valued and encouraged in Islamic teachings. It signifies someone who is not only self-reliant, but also extends a helping hand to others. This notion is deeply embedded in the principle of 'khilafa' or 'khalifa', which translates to 'vicegerent' or 'caliph', in the Islamic context. As Muslims believe that every person is a vicegerent of Allah on Earth, it becomes an individual's responsibility to help and support others, just as Allah would.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Budaid" signifies one who is not only connected to their Creator but also extends that connection to other beings. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Whoever relieves a believer's distress in this world, Allah will relieve his distress on the Day of Resurrection." This Hadith encourages providing help and relief, not only to maintain social harmony but also as an act of worship to Allah. By bearing the name 'Budaid', one is constantly reminded of the importance of supporting and assisting others, as well as Allah's guidance and blessings upon that individual in their undertakings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Helper" symbolizes One who assists, a helper, a supporter. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Budaid serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of helper.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Al-Athir, Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh. Vol. 4, p. 12. Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr. p. 146. The name Budaid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Budaid ibn Dhghiath was an Egyptian Bedouin chief who allied himself with the Fatimid caliph al-Mustalsam bi-llah (r. 1036-1045). He helped the caliph in several military campaigns against the Seljuq Turks. After defeating a Seljuq army near Damietta, Budaid was rewarded with the title 'Emir of the Jazira'.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr. p. 284. The name Budaid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Later, Budaid revolted against the Fatimid caliph al-Mustansir bi-llah (r. 1036-1094), taking advantage of a power vacuum caused by the Mongol invasion. He proclaimed himself as the new ruler of Egypt. However, his rebellion was soon put down by the Fatimid general Sharaf al-Din al-Hardani.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Budaid' is of Islamic origin and is believed to derive from the Arabic word 'Budud,' meaning 'the one who throws stones.' In modern contexts, this name is often associated with Islamic history, as it was the name of an early Muslim tribe known for their bravery and military prowess. On platforms such as Wikipedia, Instagram, and Reddit, one can find various discussions, articles, and visual representations of the Budaid tribe and their significance in Islamic history. Additionally, the name 'Budaid' is also seen in the context of Arabic names, as it is a unique and evocative name for both boys and girls. In Islamic art and culture, the name 'Budaid' may be depicted in various forms, such as calligraphy, illuminated manuscripts, or as part of Islamic geometric patterns. Overall, the name 'Budaid' is a fascinating glimpse into Islamic history and culture, and its modern usage is a testament to the enduring interest in and appreciation for this rich tradition.
